title: 상황별 인사말: 언제, 누구에게, 어떻게 말해요?
objective: By the end, you can find the right greeting in a list for a given situation, and change it to the right speech level for a senior or a close friend.
summary: A short guide to Korean greetings for work, holidays, meals, illness and goodbyes, with polite and casual forms for different listeners.
note: This list shows greetings Koreans use every day, sorted by situation and by who you are talking to.

task.title: Choose the right greeting
task.line: Read the situation, think about who the listener is, and pick or write the greeting that fits.

items.text: Say it when you leave work while your boss or coworkers are still there.

items.gloss: thank you for your hard work
items.text: Say it to coworkers or people younger than you when a day's work or a task is finished. Some people feel it is rude to a boss or elder, so use 고생 많으셨습니다 for them.
items.example: 민수 씨, 오늘 발표 준비하느라 수고하셨습니다.

items.text: Use it around 1 January and Seollal (Lunar New Year), especially to older people.
Say it before Seollal or Chuseok, when people go home to their families.
items.example: 다음 주가 추석이네요. 즐거운 명절 보내세요.

items.text: 생신 is the honorific word for 생일; use it for parents, grandparents or a boss.
Say it to someone who is sick or hurt.
Say it on the last day, when you leave a job, class or group.
items.example: 오늘이 마지막 수업이네요. 선생님, 그동안 감사했습니다.

items.text: Say it before eating, especially when someone else pays or cooks.
Use it to end a phone call or to say goodbye to someone older; it does not mean 'go inside'.

sections.heading: 같은 인사, 다른 말투
paragraphs: Same situation, different listener. To a senior: 고생 많으셨습니다 / 새해 복 많이 받으세요 / 얼른 나으세요. To a close friend or someone younger: 수고했어 / 새해 복 많이 받아 / 얼른 나아. Honorific words change too: 생신 → 생일, 드리다 → 하다.

sections.heading: 문화 팁: 한국 인사 문화
paragraphs: Many Koreans avoid saying 수고하세요 to a boss, because it can sound like telling them to keep working. When you leave first, say 먼저 들어가 보겠습니다 instead.
'밥 먹었어요?' is often just a friendly hello, not an invitation to eat. A short answer like '네, 먹었어요' is enough.

exercises: Choose the right greeting: 저녁 6시예요. 팀장님은 아직 일하고 계세요. 나는 지금 집에 가요. (a) 팀장님, 수고하세요. (b) 팀장님, 먼저 들어가 보겠습니다.
Write the greeting for each situation: ① 설날 아침에 큰아버지께 ② 친구가 독감에 걸려서 학교에 못 왔어요. 친구에게 문자로 ③ 3년 동안 다닌 회사를 그만두는 날, 동료들에게
Change the greeting for a close friend: 할머니, 생신 축하드립니다. → 지수야, ____.
Fill in the blank: 부장님이 오늘 저녁을 사 주셨어요. 먹기 전에 → 부장님, 잘 ____.
True or False: ① 전화를 끊을 때 '들어가세요'는 'Please go inside.'라는 뜻이에요. ② '밥 먹었어요?'는 인사로 자주 써요. ③ 친한 친구에게는 '추석 잘 보내세요'보다 '추석 잘 보내'가 더 자연스러워요.
answers: ① 새해 복 많이 받으세요. ② 얼른 나아. (빨리 나아.) ③ 그동안 감사했습니다.
① False ② True ③ True
